Bo stands in the river and — SPLASH! — catches a fish.
Bo finds a bush full of sweet berries. Munch, munch, munch!
Bo’s tummy is full and Bo is sleepy. Soon it will be winter — time for the long sleep in a cozy den. Goodnight, Bo!
Did you know? Many brown bears spend the coldest months resting in a den.
Did you know? Brown bears eat many different foods, including berries, plants, insects and fish.
Hazel runs up the tree trunk — zip, zip, zip!
Hazel buries nuts in the ground to eat later. One here… one there…
Hazel curls up in a round nest of twigs and moss, her bushy tail like a blanket. Goodnight, Hazel!
Did you know? Squirrels bury nuts for later — the forgotten ones can grow into new trees!
Did you know? A squirrel’s bushy tail is a blanket and helps it balance.
Luna and the pack wake up together. Lick, sniff — good morning, family!
The wolf pups play tag in the grass while Luna watches.
Under the moon, Luna howls to call the family home. Ahoooo! Goodnight, Luna!
Did you know? Wolves howl to talk to their family, even far away.
Did you know? Wolves live in families called packs.
Shhh… Kiri is fast asleep in a cozy burrow. Many kiwis rest in the daytime and search for food at night.
Still sleeping… snore… Kiri is saving energy for tonight.
Night time! Kiri wakes up and sniffs the ground with a long beak to find wiggly worms. Good morning… I mean, goodnight, Kiri!
Did you know? Kiwis have nostrils at the very tip of their beak!
Did you know? A kiwi is a bird that can’t fly.
Fen sleeps in a cool burrow under the sand, away from the hot sun.
The desert is SO hot. Fen stays underground and waits.
The desert cools down. Fen’s giant ears listen for little bugs. Goodnight, Fen!
Did you know? Fennec foxes have very large ears for their size — they help them stay cool!
Did you know? Fennec foxes have furry feet so the hot sand doesn’t burn them.
Nico is asleep in a pile of soft leaves. Zzz…
Still asleep… Hedgehogs are mostly active after dark.
Snuffle, snuffle! Nico looks for beetles in the garden. A noise! Nico rolls into a spiky ball. Goodnight, Nico!
Did you know? A hedgehog has thousands of spines on its back!
Did you know? When scared, a hedgehog rolls into a spiky ball.
Mist floats on the lake. People wait with cameras. Is that a long neck in the water? Or just a log?
A big ripple goes across the lake… then nothing. Nessie is very, very shy!
The lake is quiet and dark. Maybe Nessie is swimming deep down, dreaming. Goodnight, Nessie!
Did you know? Loch Ness is a very big, very deep lake in Scotland.
Did you know? People have looked for Nessie for many years, but there is no scientific proof she exists!
High in the snowy mountains, climbers find giant footprints. Whose feet are SO big?
The wind blows. Something fluffy and white runs behind a rock… or was it just snow?
The stars shine on the tallest mountains in the world. Goodnight, Yeti, wherever you are!
Did you know? The Himalayas have the tallest mountains in the world, like Mount Everest.
Did you know? Scientists tested some “Yeti” hair — it came from bears!
In the big forest, a hiker finds a HUGE footprint in the mud. Stomp!
Something tall and hairy walks between the trees… Is it Bigfoot? Or a bear?
The forest is quiet. Maybe Bigfoot is having a big, hairy nap. Goodnight, Bigfoot!
Did you know? Bigfoot is also called Sasquatch.
Did you know? Nobody has ever proven Bigfoot is real, but people still love to look!
The great Mekong River sparkles in the sun. People say a giant serpent lives deep below.
Fishermen tell stories of the Naga, who protects the river and its fish.
Some people report seeing mysterious lights near the river on special nights. In the legend, they say: “The Naga is sending fireballs!” Goodnight, Naga!
Did you know? In Thailand and Laos, people tell stories of the Naga, a great serpent of the Mekong River.
Did you know? Every year, crowds gather by the Mekong to watch for “Naga fireballs”.
A little rabbit hops in the grass… wait, does it have ANTLERS?
Boing! Jackie jumps over a cactus. Nobody can catch a jackalope!
Jackie hides in the tall grass, antlers and all. Goodnight, Jackie!
Did you know? The jackalope is a funny legend: a rabbit with deer antlers!
Did you know? In Douglas, Wyoming, there is a giant jackalope statue!
